model: Smoke X2 Long-Range Remote BBQ Alarm Thermometer
tier_rationale: Has a radio (FCC grants 2AI67-S2T transmitter and 2AI67-S2R receiver, 902.5-927 MHz proprietary spread-spectrum RF, not WiFi or Bluetooth) that speaks only point-to-point to a receiver the owner holds. ThermoWorks' own support documentation states no app, WiFi, or account exists for this model, and the same grantee separately files WiFi/Bluetooth grants for its connected line (Signals, BLUEDOT) — confirming Smoke X2 is deliberately the non-cloud product in the catalog, not an unfiled oversight.
the_unplug_test: There is no cloud for this device to be cut off from. The probe transmitter talks directly to its own handheld receiver over a dedicated 915 MHz radio link rated to 1.24 miles line-of-sight — the same link whether your house has internet or not. ThermoWorks explicitly states no WiFi add-on exists for this model, unlike its Signals product line.

repairability.notes: Replacement probes are sold individually by ThermoWorks; transmitter and receiver run on AA batteries or USB-C power, both user-replaceable/rechargeable.

sources.supports: Manufacturer support article: Smoke X2 uses 'an all-new RF wireless technology,' states 'A Wi-Fi enabled add-on is not available for Smoke X2' (unlike the original Smoke, which can add a WiFi gateway accessory), and confirms no account or internet connection is required for Smoke X2 to function; range up to 6,562 ft (1.24 mi) line-of-sight; 915 MHz RF; splash-proof IP66; up to 330 hours on AA batteries or USB-C powered.

FCC grant for ThermoWorks (grantee 2AI67) model S2T, the Smoke X2 transmitter: 902.5-927 MHz spread-spectrum Digital Transmission System under Part 15C, 1.4 mW output — a proprietary point-to-point RF link, not WiFi or Bluetooth. Sibling control: the same grantee (2AI67) separately holds WiFi/Bluetooth grants for its connected products (Signals, BLUEDOT 'Bluetooth thermometer'), confirming ThermoWorks files distinct grants when a product actually carries a cloud-capable radio, and Smoke X2's grant is for local-only RF instead.

open_questions: Firmware update mechanism for the transmitter/receiver pair, and whether updates can be declined, was not established within budget.

Exact current retail price varies by color/bundle and frequent promotions; $99-140 reflects the range observed across the manufacturer's own past pricing and independent retailers, not a single verified list price captured today.
notes: A clean D1 case in a category (thermometer probe) that otherwise skews heavily toward Bluetooth/WiFi cloud products (Meater, Weber iGrill, ThermoWorks' own Signals). The same manufacturer sells both kinds side by side, which makes the FCC sibling-grant comparison unusually clean.
